ai.subject: Medicine
ai.summary: Orofacial anomalies are congenital malformations of the mouth, jaws, and facial structures that affect feeding, speech, breathing, and psychosocial health. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care improve outcomes.

b: Incidence ~1 in 700 births worldwide; higher in Asian and Native American populations
Most common isolated form: cleft palate alone
sections.p: These anomalies arise from disrupted embryologic fusion of facial prominences between weeks 4‑12. They range from isolated cleft lip to complex syndromic presentations.
Classification is based on location (lip, alveolus, hard palate, soft palate) and laterality. Severity is staged by the Veau system (I‑IV).

t.b: Can a cleft be detected before birth? → Positive finding prompts counseling and delivery planning.
Is a syndromic cause likely? → Abnormal result guides further evaluation for cardiac, renal, or neuro anomalies.

b: Feeding: use specialized bottles or nasogastric feeds
Ear infections: common due to eustachian tube dysfunction
sections.p: Newborns may have feeding difficulty, nasal regurgitation, and risk of aspiration. Later, speech, hearing, dental occlusion, and psychosocial issues arise.

t.b: Is conductive hearing loss present? → Abnormal result leads to early ear tube placement.
Is airway compromise from associated micrognathia? → Positive finding may require immediate airway support.

b: Always inspect palate with a tongue depressor in newborns with facial clefts
Ask about family history and maternal exposures (e.g., smoking, folate deficiency)
Screen for cardiac defects with echocardiogram when a syndrome is suspected
sections.p: Focus on pattern recognition, associated anomalies, and the need for multidisciplinary referral.

b: Missing a submucous cleft palate because the mucosa looks intact
Neglecting to assess for associated syndromes (e.g., 22q11.2 deletion)
Relying solely on visual exam without audiology in a child with speech delay
sections.p: Avoid assuming an isolated cleft when other anomalies are hidden, and do not delay feeding support.

whenToSeekHelp: Uncontrolled feeding failure leading to dehydration
